title: Smallest Divisible Digit Product I
statement: Given two integers `n` and `t`, find the least integer `x` with `x >= n` for which multiplying together all the decimal digits of `x` gives a multiple of `t`, and return `x`. A digit product of `0` counts as a multiple of every `t`.
notes:
## Intuition

The hint is in the last digit. Among any ten consecutive integers one ends in `0`, and its digit product is `0`, which every `t` divides. So the answer is at most nine steps past `n`, and simply testing `n, n + 1, n + 2, ...` in order is already the efficient solution. The first number that passes is the smallest by construction.

## Approach

1. Start with `candidate = n`.
2. Compute the digit product: begin with `product = 1`, and while `rest > 0` multiply by its last digit `rest % 10`, then drop that digit with `Math.floor(rest / 10)`.
3. If `product % t === 0`, return `candidate`.
4. Otherwise move on to `candidate + 1` and repeat.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 10`, `t = 2`. The first candidate is `10`: its last digit is `0`, so `product = 1 · 0 = 0`, and then the digit `1` keeps it at `0`. Since `0 % 2 === 0`, the answer is `10` itself.

(Example 2: `15` has product 5 and fails for `t = 3`, while `16` has product 6 and passes.)

## Complexity

- Time: O(log n) in total: at most 10 candidates, each with O(log n) digits.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- Start at `n` itself; the answer may be `n` (Example 1).
- Start the product at `1`, not `0`, or every number would pass.
- A zero digit makes the product `0`, which counts as divisible; do not skip such numbers.
- Stop the digit loop when `rest` reaches `0`: leading zeros are not digits of the number.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `candidate` | the number being tested, starting at `n` |
| `product` | product of the digits seen so far |
| `rest` | the digits of `candidate` not yet multiplied in |

narration.2: Begin the search at n itself, since n may already work.
narration.3: Keep trying consecutive numbers; one ending in 0 is at most nine steps away.
narration.4: An empty product is 1, so multiplying in the digits starts from there.
narration.5: rest holds the digits of candidate that are still to be multiplied in.
narration.7: Multiply in the last digit of rest.
narration.10: Is the digit product a multiple of t (0 always is)?
narration.11: Yes: this is the first, so the smallest, number that works.
